audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings contain a temporary pre-tariff inventory benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily low inventory cost increased FY2025 gross profit and the $64.1 million OE anchor, which is capitalized through every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The year over year improvement resulted strategic pricing management including the timing benefit from pre-tariff inventory flowing through cost of sales and overall freight management, including both inbound and outbound logistics as well as quality initiatives that reduced freight claims and customer returns.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization issue, not merely a forecast risk: the 2025 filing identifies the timing benefit, and the 2026 filing confirms that prior-year margin benefited from temporary inventory valuation favorability. The portion attributable to that benefit is not separated from pricing, freight, claims, and returns within the 120-basis-point gross-margin improvement. Its valuation materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile gross margin by inventory-cost cohort and use 2026 post-turn results, excluding the IEEPA refund, to quantify the after-tax temporary benefit; rerun all scenarios with a normalized 52-week OE anchor.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $86.7 million, or $2.22 per share and 8.8% of the $987.0 million base equity value; $7.3 million of foreign cash, or $0.19 per share, was filed as primarily supporting local working capital
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating or otherwise unavailable cash should be removed from the $86.7 million equity bridge addition.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary liquidity needs are to support working capital requirements in our business, funding recently declared and any future dividends, funding capital expenditures and inventory purchases, continuing investment in upgrading and expanding our technological capabilities specifically related to additional functionality and enhanced navigation of our new web platform, continuing investment in sales, marketing, merchandising, customer service and upgrading our distribution footprint and funding acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The surplus-cash designation is insufficiently supported, and the filing specifically identifies cash used for working capital. Nevertheless, even removing the entire $86.7 million balance—the maximum possible correction—would reduce base value from $25.27 to about $23.05 per share and bull value from $27.96 to about $25.74, both still well below the $39.81 market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion, although it changes the reported values.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash using monthly seasonality, restricted and foreign balances, outstanding checks, and committed uses; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: The tariff regime changed after the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.2 million total IEEPA refunds: $21.1 million credited to cost of sales, $1.1 million to interest income, and $4.0 million to inventory; filed after-tax benefit $16.4 million, or $0.42 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 tariff costs depressed the $64.1 million OE anchor, while the later refund was divided among cash, receivables, inventory, cost of sales, and interest and was not incorporated into normalized anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: This decision invalidated the tariffs imposed by the President under the IEEPA during 2025, of which the Company paid a material amount on items imported.
audit_findings.explanation: The post-anchor change and refund are demonstrated. The $16.4 million after-tax benefit equals 25.6% of anchor OE. Mechanically capitalizing that amount on the same base-case relationship would increase value by approximately $230.5 million, or $5.90 per share, which is large enough to materially alter the fair-value range even though it would not by itself lift base value above the $39.81 market price. The proper recurring adjustment remains unresolved because the refund is nonrecurring and new Section 301 tariffs became effective in July 2026.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE without the invalidated IEEPA costs, exclude refund income and interest as nonrecurring, reconcile the $26.2 million among cash, receivable, and inventory to prevent double counting, and separately model the ongoing Section 301 cost run rate before rerunning valuation.

audit_findings.title: The latest-quarter liabilities side of the bridge is not fully closed
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $0.0 million debt, $1.6 million letters of credit, and $0.9 million other liabilities; the latter two total $2.5 million, or $0.06 per share and 0.25% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted June 2026 senior claim would require a bridge deduction if it were not already reflected in OE or operating working capital.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, eligible collateral under the credit agreement was $125.0 million, total availability was $122.1 million, total outstanding letters of credit was $1.6 million, total excess availability was $120.5 million and there were no outstanding borrowings.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied June 2026 filing closes the principal uncertainty: the balance sheet reports liabilities, management states that no debt was outstanding, and the renewed facility reports $121.4 million availability, $1.6 million letters of credit, and $119.8 million excess availability. The $98.9 million lease liability is already disclosed as context under the stated equity-OE method. No omitted borrowing or other material senior claim is demonstrated; even treating the filed letters of credit and other liabilities as additional bridge claims would reduce value by only about $0.06 per share.
audit_findings.action: Retain the June 2026 balance-sheet and facility reconciliation in the audit record; rerun the bridge only if confirmation identifies restricted cash, acquisition consideration, finance debt, or another senior claim not already recorded.

audit_findings.title: Indoff's financial-reporting controls remain materially weak
audit_findings.mechanism: An undetected Indoff error could affect reported income, inventory, accruals, working-capital adjustments, and therefore historical or anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the evaluation, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of December 31, 2025, the Company’s disclosure controls and procedures were not effective due to material weaknesses identified at its subsidiary, Indoff LLC (Indoff), which represents approximately 13% of revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The control weakness is demonstrated and remained unresolved at June 30, 2026, when Indoff represented approximately 12% of revenue. It is not a demonstrated valuation-input error: management found no misstatement, performed additional procedures, and the 2025 financial statements received an unqualified opinion. Indoff produced filed 2025 revenue of $174.9 million and net income of $5.2 million, but those figures do not quantify any error or Indoff's contribution to OE, so valuation materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain completion and operating-effectiveness testing for the redesigned Indoff controls and independently reconcile Indoff revenue, inventory, receivables, accruals, and working-capital cash flows to the consolidated OE calculation; rerun only for identified adjustments.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor includes an extra operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: mechanical 52/53 normalization reduces anchor OE by $1.21 million and base equity value by approximately $17.0 million, or $0.44 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The extra week increases the annual OE anchor and is perpetuated through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The full year of 2025 included 53 weeks and full years of 2024 and 2023 included 52 weeks.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53-week distortion is demonstrated. Under a mechanical 52/53 normalization, base value falls from $25.27 to approximately $24.83 per share, bull value falls by approximately $0.49 to $27.47, and the 30% margin-of-safety threshold falls by about $0.31. These changes are small relative to the $14.54 gap between market price and base value and cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a selling-day and week-specific normalization of sales, margins, and working capital and record a 52-week sensitivity rerun; retain the current investment conclusion unless that detailed calculation materially exceeds the mechanical adjustment.
